web_bottleneck: Brookfield relieves the capital bottleneck: on 2026-09-17 Flatt said the banking system lacks capacity for the tens of trillions of AI and power build-out, forcing private credit (Investor Day transcript). Its own bottlenecks are deploying 210B USD at 15 pct plus returns without overpaying and sourcing scarce long-lead power equipment.
web_who_benefits_next: Second-order winners: hyperscalers and NVIDIA (Naver is buying 10B USD of NVIDIA chips, Flatt 2026-09-17); Westinghouse; Bloom Energy; grid and power-equipment suppliers; data-center landlords; insurers such as Just Group; and listed affiliates BIP and BEP (GlobeNewswire 2026-08-13).
web_who_loses: Rival alternative and private-credit managers (Apollo, KKR, Blackstone, Ares) lose share and fee pricing as Brookfield scales 672B USD of fee-bearing capital (2026-08-13). Banks lose infrastructure lending capacity and fees. Chinese power-equipment vendors lose US nuclear and battery share. Public-market yield buyers lose allocations to private assets.
